I’ve been an Overcast user for years and years, it’s been my podcast player for most of my adult life and I have had a 5 star review on this bad boy since the beginning. I love this podcast player.

I’m downgrading the review to a 3 though because lately the app feels like it’s become much buggier. Audio often stops playing even while the podcast ticks down. Swipe actions also often trigger interaction so deleting episodes first plays them. Download failures, there’s a memory leak on the search screen where if you search, exit, and open search again you get your old search.

It’s still a great podcast player but it doesn’t feel all that reliable anymore. I hope it’s temporary and I’ll back here again with a 5 star review in a few months!

This is the best podcast player on the market. I pay for the yearly subscription and it’s completely worth it. Recently they added a much needed customizable EQ and it works excellent.
This is the best podcast app; it works flawlessly. I prefer it over the other podcast apps, and yes I’ve tried them all.

If you’re tired of all the extra recommendation junk clogging up Apple’s app, just give Overcast a try. The recommendations are still there when you want to search for something, but not cluttering things up when you just want to listen to your podcasts. You also have the ability to customize the already great interface. I was a long-time holdout sticking to the stock app, but I finally gave it a try and now I don’t want to go back to being bombarded by Apple’s recommendations. 

I have also discovered a whole world of other features that I didn’t realize existed whether that is the option to reduce spaces which speed ups listening without missing content, select specific chapters for selective listening, and much more. Some of the features are behind a small paywall, but just the normal great, better than Apple, podcast player is free with reasonable ads for podcasts you might actually want to check out.

I listen to A LOT of podcasts. I’ve used A LOT of podcast apps, on Android and iOS, over more than a decade. This is the best podcast app I’ve ever used. This is the podcast app you’ve been wanting and searching for, even if you didn’t realize it. Everything about it is outstanding. Most features work perfectly right out of the box, but if they don’t, changing them to the way you want is quick and simple. It’s free to try. Just get the app. You won’t regret it.

[Update at iOS 27 launch time]

Among the fantastic recent improvements, a huge standout for me is podcast transcriptions. The best part is they are tappable. 

Has Leo started an eleven minute commercial on a show with no chapter markers? No problem! Tap the paragraph after the ad and the podcast jumps there! No need to skip 30 seconds and wonder if this is the real end of the ad or one of four or five false endings. No more sitting through twenty repeats of the URL. Thank you Marco! Now can you make him stop talking over everyone?

[End update]

Marco has mocked people like me who haven't switched to iOS 7 yet. Ironically, this app might be what finally makes me take the plunge. 

I set it up on my iPad and now I don't think I can listen to podcasts in the car without it. Varying voice volume drives me batty in the car because the quiet people force me to turn it up and then the loud people are painful. This app completely solves that. Plus, it goes faster than 2x, so slow-talkers are no longer a problem. 

WARNING: Do not listen to Merlin Mann faster than 2x. You'll start to buzz and disappear like those people on Star Trek. 

The app can use some refinements, like being able to go back to where you left off in adding podcasts instead of starting at the beginning, but it is really a first-class app. Buy it now.

title.label: Episode Limits Broken and Stress Inducing

content.label: Look, I get that for whatever reason, people did not like episode limit strictness. I personally don’t understand why a strict opinion was even necessary. If a limit is set by a user, then respect it. Period. Now it seems that setting an episode limit has little impact. Among my podcasts, I listen to a few that are news and opinion, and they also have hourly updates. I only ever want to listen to the latest. Now I can’t. Now I have to manually delete or fast forward through older ones (i.e in the car) after the latest finished playing. This is such a basic function that needs to work - even with automatic downloads - that I am now looking at other players or will just use Apple Podcasts. Seriously. I am also unsubscribing because it’s bad enough that an app causes stress and distraction by having to actively work around it (especially when driving). I am certainly not going to pay for that even if the sub isn’t that pricy.

title.label: If you're looking for a podcast app, this is it

content.label:
It's unbelievably, blessedly customizable, but not overly technical. The interface isn't cluttered or cumbersome. It's free but the ads aren't intrusive. It's got a massive library and the recommendations aren't promotional or otherwise irrelevant. There are no shareholders and using it doesn't fund terrible things. You don't feel forced into a subscription, either by excessive ads or by downgrades in the free experience, but Premium still has cool features I'm interested in (plus it supports the app.) Personally, I love that it doesn't try to be a social platform either.

I honestly have no idea how one guy made such a perfect app in his spare time.
Deleting my prior review to now account for the fact that Marco listened to feedback and fixed the episode limits.

This app has a few banner ads which you can pay to remove but it's not built to try to influence your podcast choices and that makes it better than the vast majority of other apps including the standard apple one.

Update: Aug 28, 2026

Curated downloads are fixed and will not delete after adding to a playlist. Thank you. Old review below: 

This update including a “strict episode limit” that straight up deletes episodes in progress from both my device and any playlists they’re queued in. It’s now impossible to queue up arbitrary episodes in a playlist without basically disabling the limit entirely.

The old system would occasionally delete queued up episodes as well, but they would at least be maintained in playlists and could be “pinned” by playing a few seconds of them, locking them from being downloaded.

I’m updating this review to 1-star until this change is reverted. It completely breaks playlists and makes it impossible to manually curate episodes to listen to.

title.label: Cautiously optimistic after some recent bumps (premium user)

content.label:
Aug 2026: I’m glad to still be part of this big, passionate community as a premium user. I am super grateful the dev listened and pivoted so quickly after a recent major update caused some of us to lose our queued episodes and portions of our libraries. The dev has posted on reddit they’ll move more cautiously in the future when rolling out big changes. 

I do think some folks like me are a little weary of how the dev’s evangelism for AI tools and his trust in them is likely outpacing their actual capabilities. Hopefully more guardrails are put in place?

Why am I keeping it at 4 stars? Users shouldn’t have to be in a discord or on reddit or in test flight to be able to use an app. The dev could be so much better at communicating to users within the boundaries of the app’s text and interface. Also, I’m not sure if it’s changes to voice boost or an aspect of the downloads, but some quality of the audio experience has changed. I used to be able to listen to overcast for hours each day no problem (way longer than apple podcasts) and my ears throw in the towel a lot faster now.
